facts.raw_span: 1-week history of painful vision loss and floaters in her left eye
no history of myopia, ocular trauma, or surgery
Visual acuity was 20/30–2 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye
intraocular pressure was 21 mm Hg OD and 17 mm Hg OS
mild nuclear sclerotic cataract and no inflammation in the right eye
rare anterior chamber cells, 1+ vitreous cells, choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery, and an overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid in the left eye
no retinal breaks were identified
Laboratory studies (CBC, basic metabolic panel, HIV, T-spot, syphilis screen, and ANCA panel) were normal
MRI of the brain and orbits showed mild posterior scleral enhancement but no intraocular mass
Fluorescein angiography showed late leakage in the temporal periphery
fundus autofluorescence was normal
optical coherence tomography revealed shallow subretinal fluid and a posterior vitreous detachment

concepts.why: The patient presented with painful vision loss, rare anterior chamber cells, and 1+ vitreous cells, which are consistent with posterior scleritis, and MRI showed mild posterior scleral enhancement.
The patient had a retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid and no retinal breaks, which is consistent with serous retinal detachment.
The patient had rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells, which are signs of uveitis, and laboratory studies were normal, which rules out other causes of inflammation.
The patient had a posterior vitreous detachment, which is a common condition that can cause floaters and vision loss.
The patient had choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery, which is consistent with choroidal detachment.
The patient had a mild nuclear sclerotic cataract in the right eye, which is a common age-related condition.

rationales.F01: Painful vision loss and floaters suggest posterior segment inflammation, which is consistent with posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment.
rationales.F05: Mild nuclear sclerotic cataract is a common finding in older adults, but its presence does not rule out other conditions.
rationales.F06: The presence of rare anterior chamber cells, vitreous cells, choroidal detachments, and retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid is highly suggestive of posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment.
rationales.F09: Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI is consistent with posterior scleritis, but the absence of an intraocular mass helps to rule out other conditions such as uveitis.
rationales.F12: The presence of shallow subretinal fluid and a posterior vitreous detachment on optical coherence tomography is consistent with serous retinal detachment and vitreous detachment.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms and findings, including rare anterior chamber cells, 1+ vitreous cells, choroidal detachments, and an overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid, along with MRI showing mild posterior scleral enhancement, are most consistent with posterior scleritis, which explains the decisive findings without strong contradiction.
